title: Hastening Report: Sister Camille Johnson to be Grand Marshall of the Days of '47 Parade; Photos of
text:
This week, as Utah celebrates Pioneer Day with Relief Society General President Camille N. Johnson leading the Days of ’47 Parade, we are reminded that pioneering is far more than a chapter in history. From historic Nauvoo to Brazil, Papua New Guinea, Tonga, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, faithful Saints continue to build the kingdom, strengthen communities, and carry the restored gospel to the ends of the earth. Here are nine stories that remind us that the spirit of the pioneers is alive and well today.
ONE
President Camille N. Johnson Will Lead Utah’s 2026 Pioneer Day Parade
Tuesday, July 21, 2026
Church Leadership
Relief Society General President Camille N. Johnson will be the grand marshal of Utah’s 2026 Days of ’47 Parade in Salt Lake City on Friday, July 24, 2026 (Pioneer Day in Utah). President Johnson will be joined by her husband, Doug. President Johnson, a descendant of pioneers who came to the Salt Lake Valley in the 1800s, said she draws strength from her ancestry. “I know there are pioneers all over the world pioneering in their own ways,” she continued. “I think we ought to emulate the qualities of those early pioneers who were tenacious, sought unity in their efforts and remained faithful to the gospel of Jesus Christ.” READ STORY HERE.
TWO
A Look at Historic Nauvoo in Pictures
Friday, July 17, 2026
Church History
Nauvoo, located on the banks of the Mississippi River in central Illinois, United States of America, is an important historic site of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and a piece of Americana. The city now has a new Nauvoo Temple Visitors’ Center, dedicated on June 27, 2026, where guests can learn about the importance of houses of the Lord in the restored gospel of Jesus Christ. More than 30 historic buildings have been restored or reconstructed in Nauvoo to honor the early pioneers, with more than 20 open to the public. SEE PICTURES AND STORY HERE.
THREE
Elder Cook and Elder Gilbert Minister Across the United Kingdom
Tuesday, June 23, 2026
Apostolic Ministry
From London to Preston and Oxford to Edinburgh, Elder Quentin L. Cook and Elder Clark G. Gilbert of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles spent a week ministering throughout the United Kingdom, strengthening members, meeting with faith and civic leaders and testifying of Jesus Christ. During their recent visit to the United Kingdom, the two Apostles participated in interfaith discussions, met with senior political leaders, visited sites of historic significance to the Church, met with young adults from across Europe, and addressed thousands of members and friends of the Church. SEE VIDEO AND READ STORY HERE.
FOUR
Young Single Adults Gather in Montreal to Strengthen Faith and Build Community
Tuesday, July 21, 2026
Chosen Generation
Young adults from across Eastern Canada gathered in Montreal, Quebec, June 26–28, 2026, for a weekend conference of worship, service, learning and connection hosted by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The conference gave the young adults opportunities to attend the Montreal Quebec Temple, serve in the community, participate in workshops, enjoy some recreation and build friendships with peers navigating a pivotal stage of life. The weekend also included a devotional with Elder Vern P. Stanfill, General Authority Seventy and president of the Canada Area, who spoke to attendees and answered questions. READ STORY HERE.
FIVE
Groundbreaking Date for the Maceió Brazil Temple
Monday, July 20, 2026
Temples Rising
The First Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints has announced that the groundbreaking ceremony for the Maceió Brazil Temple will be held on Saturday, October 10, 2026. Elder B. Corey Cuvelier of the Brazil Area Presidency will preside at the event. Maceió will be the sixth house of the Lord under construction in Brazil. The country has 11 dedicated temples currently. Over 1.5 million Latter-day Saints call Brazil home. READ STORY HERE.
SIX
Church Donates Student Desks and Chairs to Support Education in Tonga
Thursday, July 16, 2026
Humanitarian Outreach
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, in partnership with the Ministry of Education and Training, officially handed over the first phase of a donation of student desks and chairs during a special ceremony held at the Ministry of Education and Training’s ʻApi Mataka headquarters on Thursday, 16 July 2026. Speaking on behalf of the Church, President Uinitoni Kakau, President of the Nukuʻalofa Tonga Central Stake, reaffirmed the Church’s commitment to supporting education and strengthening communities. President Kakau explained that the donation consists of 400 small student tables and 400 small student chairs, as well as 600 regular-sized desks and 600 regular-sized chairs, all of which will be donated to Tupou College Toloa. Following his remarks, the donated furniture was formally presented to Her Royal Highness Crown Princess Sinaitakala Tukuʻaho. READ STORY HERE.
SEVEN
Fourteen Young People from Same Remote Congregation All Decide to Serve as Missionaries
Monday, July 20, 2026
To All the World
A group of fourteen young adults from the remote village of Kuriva in Papua New Guinea are part of the all-time high 88,500+ missionaries of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints sharing the gospel of Jesus Christ worldwide. They have been assigned to serve in Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Philippines, Tonga, New Zealand and Ghana. Missionaries volunteer for 18 to 24 months and are assigned to labour in one of over 500 missions globally. READ STORY HERE.
EIGHT
From BYU–Hawaii to Fiji: Building a Future Back Home
Tuesday, July 16, 2026
In the News
Leaving behind established careers, a steady income and the familiarity of home was not an easy decision for Iosefo Taliu and his wife, Grace Taliu (née Tueli).
Before moving to Hawaii, both worked as Air Traffic Control Assistants in Fiji, where they first met. They were raising two young children and building their careers when they chose to pursue higher education at Brigham Young University–Hawaii. After completing their studies, the couple recently returned home to Fiji, where their story was featured by Fiji One News. READ STORY AND SEE NEWS VIDEO CLIP HERE.
NINE
Growing Opportunities Help Australia’s Deaf Community Worship, Learn and Belong
Thursday, July 9, 2026
Humanitarian Outreach
When Lisa Atkinson joined The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, there were no Australian Sign Language (Auslan) interpreters. Each Sunday, she relied on written notes, lip reading and fragments of conversation to understand what was being taught. While hearing members listened, laughed and learned together, much of the message passed her by. Today, stories like Lisa’s are beginning to change. READ STORY HERE.
